thread:
maria: Heads-up — I noticed the console quota panel shows both v1 and v2 token counts when a tenant has a route pinned to v1. Looks like double-counting in the per-route billing view. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: I think I've seen something like that. Intended behavior was to show raw signals + final route, but UIs might be summing both. Could be a dashboard aggregation bug.

taylor: I can repro locally. If the client header is missing the request, the router emits a fallback tag (v2) then the pinned route actually serves the response; both telemetry tags end up in the same time window and the console aggregation sums by model_tag AND by final_route which creates overlap.

lee: That's bad for billing and alerting. We need a deterministic attribution policy. My vote: attribute tokens for quota/billing to the variant that actually produced the output (final_variant).

maria: +1. Also the console UX needs to expose the attribution rule and an example so tenant owners know what they're being billed for. Right now the metric name is ambiguous.

sam: Implementation idea: add a post-processing step in the telemetry pipeline that emits an "attributed_token" metric (single number) while preserving raw signals for debugging. That avoids breaking historical pipelines if we treat the derived metric as canonical for billing.

taylor: I like keeping raw + derived. UI should default to showing attributed metrics for billing/quotas and offer a toggle "Show raw signals" for troubleshooting. Hover copy explains the difference.

maria: Proposed hover copy draft: "Attributed tokens: tokens charged to the model variant that produced the final output. Raw signals: all telemetry tags emitted during the request lifecycle (used for debugging routing/fallbacks)." Thoughts?

lee: Ops note: rollout should be gated with a tenant flag. Collect 2 weeks of both metrics, run a backfill compare, and check for edge cases (e.g., cache warmup flows that emit transient tags).

maria: Good call. One tricky case: what if runtime spins up v2 transiently to warm caches but v1 returns the final tokens? Attribution should still credit v1. We need the telemetry to include final_variant + attribution_reason so we can handle these cases deterministically.

taylor: Agreed. We should capture both initial_route and final_variant and a reason enum: {"direct","fallback","cache_warmup","proxy_swap"}. That lets the console explain why attribution chose a variant.

sam: Schema example for telemetry event I'm proposing:

```json
{
  "request_id": "req-123",
  "initial_route": "v1",
  "final_variant": "v1",
  "fallback_used": false,
  "attribution_reason": "direct",
  "attributed_tokens": 420
}
```

maria: That looks good. Taylor — can you mock the console card? It should show: Attributed tokens (default), Raw tokens (toggle), Attribution reason timeline (tooltip).

taylor: Yes. I'll put together a mock with a small diff chart showing raw vs. attributed and a compact legend that explains reasons in plain language (no infra jargon).

deploy-bot: deploy-check: telemetry schema change + pipeline transform + billing job touchpoints detected. Recommend two-phase deploy: 1) ingest + derived metrics behind feature flag, 2) console UX + flag flip after validation.

lee: Timeline suggestion: flag on in staging -> 2 weeks collection in a shadow cohort -> run automated comparisons (script: compare_attributed_vs_raw.py) -> if within threshold, flip for everyone and notify finance.

maria: Action items: Sam own telemetry pipeline RFC/PR, Taylor own console mocks and copy, Lee own rollout runbook. I'll collate the UX copy and send to finance for signoff on billing attribution.

sam: Ack — I'll open RFC and a telemetry PR that adds final_variant and attribution_reason fields, plus a derived attributed_tokens metric.

taylor: Ack — I'll upload Figma mocks and a short copy doc.

lee: Ack — I'll start the rollout runbook and draft the automated comparison script.

maria: Thanks all. Tagging @ops-bot in case we need alerts on the billing side when we flip. :eyes:

ops-bot: noted. Will create a watch and notify #finance when the feature_flag is flipped.

maria: One more note — can we ensure the billing job uses the attributed_tokens metric and falls back to raw tokens only when attributed_tokens missing? We don't want a gap.

sam: Yeah, pipeline will write attributed_tokens into the same time-series namespace with a companion raw.tokens series. Billing will prefer attributed_tokens if present. We'll include safe fallback logic in the billing job.

maria: Great. I'll file a short RFC and link all the artifacts. Thanks! :thumbsup:
